text:
Maria: Heads up — we're seeing long-lived gRPC streams (chat sessions) get dropped after ~90-120s when routed through the edge LB in eu-west. Short RPCs are fine, only persistent streams hit it. Repro in staging and prod.

Kevin: Any error lines or envoy/ALB traces? RSTs / GOAWAYs?

Maria: Logs show repeated patterns like:
```
[2026-02-15T12:33:01Z] http2: stream 15 error: CANCEL
[2026-02-15T12:33:02Z] connection terminated: GOAWAY last_stream_id=55 error_code=0 debug=drain
[2026-02-15T12:33:02Z] client disconnected, reason=idle_timeout
```

Ashish: That screams proxy idle/connection drain. What are our LB/edge timeouts and client keepalive intervals?

Maria: Edge (ALB fronting Envoy) looks like this snippet from the terraform module we use:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" {
  protocol = "HTTPS"
  default_action { type = "forward" }
  # idle_timeout is not explicitly set here, default AWS ALB = 60s
}
# envoy listener uses http2 with default connection_idle_timeout = 60s in the mesh config
```

Kevin: ALB default idle is 60s. Our clients are currently configured to send HTTP/2 keepalives/pings every 120s — so the LB thinks the connection is idle and will send GOAWAY/drain. That matches the ~90-120s window you're seeing (LB+proxy timers interacting).

SRE-Bot: DeployBot noticed an autoscale event at 2026-02-15T12:34:20Z that changed egress nodes for the edge pool. Could be coincident with the spike.

Ashish: Possible root causes: mismatched keepalive vs proxy idle, ALB doing TLS termination and treating h2 as idle, or healthcheck/drain behavior during autoscale. Mitigations:
- Increase ALB/Envoy idle_timeout > client keepalive (e.g., 300s)
- Reduce client keepalive to < idle timeout (easier for client teams)
- Use TCP passthrough for long-lived streams so LB doesn't apply http idle semantics
- Add application-level HTTP/2 PINGs every 30s from clients/servers

Kevin: For immediate mitigation I'll open an infra ticket to bump ALB idle_timeout and Envoy connection_idle_timeout to 300s and add a synthetic probe that keeps streams alive. Will monitor GOAWAY/stream-cancel metrics.

Maria: Client config excerpt: `grpc.keepalive_time_ms = 120000` and server enforces a `max_connection_age = 300000` (so server is more tolerant). The mismatch was on client->edge side.

Ashish: Two notes — 1) If the LB terminates TLS it will not forward HTTP/2 PING frames, so app-level PINGs matter (gRPC keepalive uses HTTP/2 PING, but some proxies strip them). 2) Autoscale/drain sequences can trigger GOAWAY for in-flight streams even with longer timeouts; add graceful drain that waits for active stream count to go zero or a longer drain timeout.

Maria: For canary: I'll push a client patch to emit an application-level PING every 30s (non-blocking) and enable reconnect/backoff. Then Kevin can roll the ALB idle timeout change tonight.

Kevin: INFRA-1972 created. I'll add a dashboard for GOAWAYs per edge pool and wire alerts.

DeployBot: [deploy] canary client patch pushed to staging at 2026-02-15T18:05:12Z :rocket:

Maria: Confirmed staging streams stable after canary for 45m. No GOAWAYs so far.

Ashish: Long-term: move long-lived h2 traffic to TCP passthrough or ensure proxy preserves PING frames and supports longer idle windows. Filing follow-ups for connection draining behaviour on autoscale.

Kevin: Thanks — we'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

Maria: Thanks all. Assigning followups: INFRA-1972 (idle-timeout bump + dashboard) -> Kevin, CLIENT-459 (client ping + retry) -> Maria, INFRA-1973 (drain behaviour investigation) -> Ashish.

Kevin: Acknowledged.

SRE-Bot: Incident closed (no user-facing errors) — marking as mitigated.
